content: If you are receiving ertapenem via injection into a muscle, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any allergies to amide-type local anesthetics, such as lidocaine. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Ertapenem can interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Additionally, this medication can pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the way your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is important to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as a complete blood count or kidney function tests, to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Be sure to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. It is crucial to take each dose as scheduled to ensure the medication's effectiveness. For storage, consult the product instructions or your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Ertapenem is used to prevent and treat a variety of bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of antibiotics known as carbapenems. Before using this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist, if available. This medication is administered by injection into a muscle or vein as directed by your doctor, typically once or twice daily. If it is being used to prevent an infection, it is usually given by injection into a vein by a healthcare professional. If the medication is administered into a muscle, follow the manufacturer's instructions for mixing it with a 1% lidocaine solution. If you are using this medication at home, ensure you understand all preparation and usage instructions provided by your healthcare professional. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed treatment period, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site, as well as upset stomach, headache, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using ertapenem, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other carbapenems (e.g., imipenem), penicillins, cephalosporins, or any other substances. If you are receiving this medication via injection into a muscle, also inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to any amide-type local anesthetics, such as lidocaine. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ertapenem may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication also passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
